The *Tevijja Sutta* (Iti 99; It 3.50, PTS It 98), titled *Tevijjasutta* and translated by Bhikkhu Sujato as "The Three Knowledges," belongs to the *Itivuttaka* [SuttaCentral]. The discourse redefines the traditional Brahmanical concept of threefold knowledge by setting forth the three higher knowledges (*tevijjā*) that characterize a true brāhmaṇa in the Buddha's sense of the term [SuttaCentral]. All secondary literature passages retrieved in the reference dossier pertain exclusively to the homonymous *Tevijja Sutta* of the *Dīgha Nikāya* (DN 13) rather than to this *Itivuttaka* discourse.

SuttaCentral notes extensive canonical and cross-tradition parallels to the text, including *Dhammapada* 423, the *Tikaṇṇasutta* (AN 3.58), the *Jāṇussoṇisutta* (AN 3.59), the *Brahmāyu Sutta* (MN 91), the *Vāseṭṭha Sutta* (MN 98; Snp 3.9), and verses in the *Brāhmaṇasaṁyutta* (SN 7.8, SN 7.13) [SuttaCentral]. Parallels outside Pali include several Chinese translations of the *Dharmapada* and related texts (T 210.35, T 212.34, T 213.33), Sanskrit recensions of the *Udānavarga* (UV 33, UVS 33), and resembling passages in the Gāndhārī *Dharmapada* (G-Dhp 1–50) and *Therīgāthā* (Thig 4.1) [SuttaCentral].
